meta.description: Installed generation capacity by province, MW. Thermal from the station-level fleet register (BASE scenario); wind and utility solar from the regional renewable capacity compilation; rooftop from the distributed PV estimate.
meta.note: CAPACITY, not generation. A province with 30 GW of coal produces far more energy than one with 3 GW of solar at the same nameplate, because the capacity factors differ by a factor of four or five. Read the energy shares alongside, never the megawatts alone.
meta.generation_note: Generation is the engine's, not measured: each technology's national total is the engine's at start-up (Today 2026, build 2026-10-21g): coal 147.2, nuclear 10.9, hydro 2.9, gas and diesel 0.9, wind 14.3, solar with rooftop 25.8 TWh. Coal, nuclear, hydro and gas are split by installed capacity; wind and solar by the regional hourly profiles (a Hydra Central wind MW at 42.5%, a KwaZulu-Natal one at 21.6%). It does not change with the scenario. National generation is 104% of demand; the gap is imports, exports and storage, which are not allocated by province. Built by harness/build_provincial_mix.js.
meta.demand_note: Provincial demand is the engine's grid demand at start-up (194.7 TWh; loadS less storage charging plus demand response) apportioned by the regional model's shares, the ten hourly columns of nodal/demand_2025_regional.csv summed (2025; that file's source and terms apply to the shares). An allocation, not a measurement.
